latest_findings.claim: At N=256 (seeds 56/57/58, 4 layers, d_model=64, best-of-5 controls, checkpoints every 10 steps), accel_step persistently formed at steps 100/160/120. Final layer-4 R2 was 0.849/0.896/0.887 against controls 0.680/0.778/0.719, giving margins of 0.169/0.118/0.168. On the threshold-free measure (first checkpoint at half of the run's final margin), formation came at steps 90/80/100, about where the N=64 runs this hypothesis cites formed (80/85/90). Force never beat its control (final margin 0.000-0.020, after a short rise to 0.16-0.19 at steps 10-30 that faded by step 80-110), and val_mse_ratio stayed at 11.3-12.8 (never below 1).
latest_findings.confidence_note: This finding covers only the N=256 arm. The per-seed N=64 formation steps for seeds 56-58 are not in these results, so the paired per-seed differences the hypothesis needs could not be computed. The comparison above uses the earlier, unmatched N=64 values (80/85/90). Against those, the two measures disagree, which the hypothesis's own rules count as inconclusive. On the 0.1-margin bar, N=256 is 10-80 steps later. Seed 57's step-160 crossing is driven by its small final margin (0.118, only just above the bar), which comes from the highest control R2 (0.778). On the half-final-margin measure, N=256 is 80-100, which is within about 10-20 steps of N=64 and points to roughly fixed timing. A raw 0.1 threshold seems to measure each seed's ceiling (set by its control R2) more than when formation happens. Formation also does not occur at a fixed fraction of step-0 val MSE: it falls at 2.3-5.5% of step-0 on the 0.1 bar and 6-9% on the half-final measure, versus about 2-3% reported at N=64. What would change the verdict: joining these runs with the matched N=64 runs on seeds 56-58. If N=64 minus N=256 on the half-final measure is within 10 steps in 2 of 3 seeds, the result moves toward refuted (timing fixed across N, and the raw-threshold gap is a ceiling artifact). If N=256 is 20 or more steps later on both measures in all seeds, the result is supported. All runs completed 300 of 300 steps.

latest_findings.claim: In both seeds of the 6-layer, d_model=128 model at e in [0, 0.85], the best-layer (layer 6) accel_step R2 levelled off at about 0.70-0.74 and only crept up after step 2000. It went from 0.710 to 0.735 in seed 56 (+0.025) and from 0.683 to 0.705 in seed 57 (+0.022), and never reached 0.8. Over the same steps val_mse_ratio kept falling 6.8x (0.0253 to 0.0037) and 5.5x (0.0177 to 0.0032). At step 4000, accel_step beats its best-of-5 control (0.229/0.239, spread <= 0.015) with margins of 0.506 and 0.465. Force is weaker: R2 0.566/0.516, margins 0.300/0.333, and its best layer drifts across layers 1-6. Its headroom-normalized margin is 0.41 in both seeds, against 0.66/0.61 for accel_step.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds ran to full completion and meet every expected-if-true criterion. Neither meets the >= 0.05 rise from the expected-if-false outcome. The accel_step margin is far above the required margin (0.1), so control noise is not an issue. Limits: (1) The plateau is not perfectly flat. R2 rises slowly and monotonically (about 0.011-0.012 per 1000 steps) and the change sits just inside the 0.03 bound, so a much longer run could still creep toward 0.8. (2) Checkpoints are 500 steps apart, so any short-lived change in between would be missed. (3) Both seeds share data_seed 0 and one architecture. (4) Separation shows that linear decodability of accel_step stops tracking prediction quality. It does not show that a nonlinear accel_step code exists. The extra accuracy could instead come from distance (R2 0.98 at layer 1) plus later nonlinear computation. I would revise the verdict if an MLP or log(accel_step) probe also plateaus near 0.7, which would point to a missing feature rather than a readout limit. I would also revise it if training to 8000+ steps pushed linear R2 past 0.8.

latest_findings.claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, best-of-5 controls, 10-step checkpoints), accel_step forms persistently at step 90, 90 and 80 in seeds 57, 58 and 56. All three fall inside the predicted [70, 100], and in every seed the margin stays at or above the 0.1 bar at every later checkpoint. Final layer-4 accel_step R2 is 0.909/0.875/0.882 against controls 0.769/0.731/0.709 (margins 0.139/0.144/0.173; headroom-normalized 0.61/0.54/0.59). Force never beats its control: final margin is 0.05-0.08 against a bar of 0.1, after a short spike at step 10 (margin 0.152-0.158) that falls to about 0 by steps 40-70. val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at steps 150/150/170, 60-90 steps after accel_step forms, ending at 0.45-0.48.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The main prediction (persistent formation step in [70, 100] in all 3 seeds) and the val_mse_ratio timing prediction (first below 1 in [130, 170], after formation) both hold in every seed. This replicates the 80-90 formation steps of f-20261012-005950-42a7 on new seeds. Two secondary numbers fall slightly outside their predicted ranges: seed 58's final R2 is 0.875 (predicted 0.88-0.91), and seed 56's control is 0.709 (predicted 0.72-0.79). Neither changes the timing result. The formation step is threshold-sensitive. At the crossing, the margin rises only about 0.01 per 10 steps, and seed 58 crosses at exactly 0.100. A bar 0.02 higher would therefore move formation by about 20 steps. Final margins are also only 0.04-0.07 above the bar, so a fixed 0.1 threshold measures timing coarsely. The cross-seed formation spread is 10 steps (80-90). The paired N=256 arm should be compared against that spread. What would change the verdict: a rerun with different probe splits or control draws that moves any seed's persistent formation step outside [70, 100], or a finding that the 0.100 crossing in seed 58 is a rounding artifact that moves its formation step to 100. 100 is still inside the range.

latest_findings.claim: With 4000 training steps, neither seed reached the pre-registered accel_step gate of R2 >= 0.8, so the hypothesis cannot be tested and the result is inconclusive. Best accel_step was at layer 6: R2 0.715 vs best-of-5 control 0.266 (margin 0.450) in seed 54, and R2 0.732 vs control 0.240 (margin 0.492) in seed 55. That is about the same as the ~0.70 the 3000-step runs (other seeds) reached, even though val_mse_ratio fell about 2.6x, from roughly 0.009 at step 3000 to 0.0035-0.0036 at step 4000. Force was weaker than accel_step at layer 3: R2 0.581/0.546 vs control 0.255/0.220 (margin 0.326 in both seeds). Headroom-normalized margin also favours accel_step in both seeds (0.61 vs 0.44 and 0.65 vs 0.42). The ungated symbolic fits did not recover a^3/r^2. Seed 54 gave 0.0127*a^2/(r+0.17)^2 (fit error 0.41) and seed 55 gave the vis-viva form a*(0.0171*a/r - 0.0088), c ≈ 0.52 (fit error 0.45). Both force fits were ~0.9/r.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 4000 steps, and their controls are tight (accel_step spread 0.012-0.020), so the margins are robust. Under the pre-registration, both seeds staying below R2 0.8 makes this inconclusive. It points toward a linear-readout limit at e <= 0.85 rather than undertraining. The undertraining explanation is weakened: next-step error kept improving about 2.6x between steps 3000 and 4000 while accel_step R2 rose by at most ~0.02-0.03. That comparison has a caveat, though. Probing was final-only, so the ~0.70 baseline at 3000 steps comes from different seeds, and we have no within-seed R2 trajectory. The symbolic fits ran below the R2 0.8 gate, so they can't confirm or refute a^3/r^2. Even so, neither shows r^-2 together with a^3, and seed 55 again gives the vis-viva form with c near 0.5. Three things would change this verdict: (a) a within-seed checkpoint trajectory showing accel_step R2 still rising at step 4000, which would favour undertraining; (b) an MLP probe or a log(accel_step) linear probe reaching >= 0.8 on these same weights, which would confirm a linear-readout limit; (c) a longer run, e.g. 8000 steps, crossing 0.8.

latest_findings.claim: At N=16, val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 at step 20 in all 3 seeds (0.80, 0.77, 0.76). That is well before accel_step reaches its required margin of 0.1 over the best-of-5 control, at step 90 for seed 47, 75 for seed 48 and 80 for seed 49. Those formation steps are 5, 15 and 5 steps from the seed-matched N=64 runs (85, 90, 85), so the 'forms before beating the baseline' ordering flips while the formation step barely moves. Final accel_step R2 at layer 4 is 0.896-0.909 against controls of 0.752-0.793 (margin 0.117-0.144, control spread under 0.011). Force is much weaker: final margins are 0.030, 0.055 and 0.123, and only seed 49 beats its control (formed at step 125). In all seeds a transient force margin of 0.106-0.127 appears at step 10 and collapses to about 0 by steps 20-30, as in the N=64 runs.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The prediction holds in 3 of 3 seeds, all trained to completion (300/300 steps), and the ordering gap is large: val_mse_ratio crosses 1 at step 20, about 55-70 steps before accel_step forms. What limits the verdict: (1) The ordering flip comes from the weaker constant-velocity baseline at N=16, not from any change in when accel_step forms. So the result mainly shows that 'val_mse_ratio < 1' is a baseline-dependent marker and should not be used to time formation across N. (2) The accel_step margin levels off just above the 0.1 bar (seed 47 reaches only 0.103 at step 90 and 0.117 at the end). At a raw 0.15 bar accel_step never forms in any seed (max 0.144), so the formation steps are sensitive to the threshold. (3) There is a small reporting inconsistency: in seed 48 the trajectory shows an accel_step margin of 0.102 at step 70, but formed_at_step is 75. Either value is inside the predicted window. (4) The N=64 comparison runs come from a separate experiment, so any difference in control sampling adds noise. The verdict would change if a headroom-normalized or fraction-of-final-margin timing measure moved N=16 formation outside [45, 130], or more than 40 steps from N=64.
